cln5.summary: CLN5 is the Dictyostelium homolog of the human neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (Batten disease) protein CLN5. It localizes to the endo-lysosomal system and has been linked to lysosomal function, protein trafficking, and autophagy; loss of cln5 perturbs cell adhesion, growth, and multicellular development, making it a tractable model for the human disease.
go: hydrolase activity, acting on glycosyl bonds

rasg.summary: rasG encodes a Ras-family small GTPase that acts as a central molecular switch in Dictyostelium, cycling between GTP- and GDP-bound states to regulate cytoskeletal dynamics, chemotaxis, cytokinesis, and growth. It functions upstream of PI3-kinase and the actin machinery during directed cell migration.

mhca.summary: mhcA encodes the conventional (class II) myosin heavy chain, the motor subunit of myosin II. As part of the actomyosin contractile machinery it drives cytokinesis, cell-shape changes, and cortical tension; mhcA-null cells fail to divide in suspension and show defects in development.

acaa.summary: acaA encodes adenylyl cyclase A, the aggregation-stage enzyme that synthesizes cyclic AMP, the key chemoattractant and developmental signal in Dictyostelium. Periodic ACA activity generates the cAMP waves that coordinate chemotactic aggregation of starving cells.

cara.summary: carA (cAR1) encodes the principal cell-surface cyclic-AMP receptor, a G-protein-coupled receptor that detects extracellular cAMP during aggregation. Through heterotrimeric G proteins it couples cAMP gradients to chemotaxis, gene expression, and the relay of cAMP signals across the developing population.

pkac.summary: pkaC encodes the catalytic subunit of cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA), a master regulator of the Dictyostelium developmental program. PKA activity controls the timing of aggregation, prestalk/prespore differentiation, and terminal spore and stalk maturation.

rega.summary: regA encodes an internal cAMP phosphodiesterase fused to a response-regulator receiver domain, integrating phosphorelay signaling with cyclic-AMP turnover. By degrading intracellular cAMP it antagonizes PKA, and its activity is tuned by the two-component system to control developmental timing.

act15.summary: act15 encodes actin, the highly abundant cytoskeletal protein whose dynamic polymerization underlies pseudopod extension, chemotaxis, phagocytosis, and cytokinesis. The act15 promoter is also widely used as a strong constitutive driver for transgene expression in Dictyostelium.

gbpc.summary: gbpC encodes the cGMP-binding protein C (GbpC), a large multidomain Roco-family protein carrying Ras-GEF, kinase and GTPase modules together with a high-affinity cGMP-binding domain. As the principal cGMP effector it links the chemoattractant-triggered cGMP signal to myosin II assembly at the cell rear, regulating cell polarity and chemotaxis to cAMP.

sada.summary: sadA (substrate adhesion deficient A) encodes a polytopic transmembrane protein essential for cell-substratum adhesion in growing Dictyostelium cells. sadA-null cells detach readily and show defects in phagocytosis and growth, identifying SadA as a core component of the substrate-adhesion machinery.

tgrb1.summary: tgrB1 encodes a polymorphic transmembrane cell-surface receptor (IPT/TIG repeats) that, together with its partner TgrC1, mediates allorecognition (kin discrimination) and the cell-cell adhesion required to progress beyond the loose-aggregate stage of development. Matching tgrB1/tgrC1 allele pairs allow cells to co-develop.

tgrc1.summary: tgrC1 (formerly LagC/gp150) encodes the cell-surface ligand for TgrB1. The TgrB1-TgrC1 receptor-ligand pair drives postaggregative cell-cell adhesion and allorecognition; tgrC1 mutants arrest in development and fail to form normal fruiting bodies.

pdsa.summary: pdsA encodes the extracellular cyclic-AMP phosphodiesterase that degrades secreted cAMP. By sharpening and resetting the extracellular cAMP signal between relay pulses it is essential for the propagating cAMP waves that organize chemotactic aggregation.

csaa.summary: csaA encodes the contact site A glycoprotein (gp80), a cell-surface adhesion molecule that mediates EDTA-resistant, homophilic cell-cell adhesion during aggregation. Its developmentally regulated expression couples starvation to the acquisition of cohesive, aggregation-competent cells.

ecma.summary: ecmA encodes an extracellular-matrix protein and is the canonical prestalk (pstA) cell-type marker in Dictyostelium. Its promoter is widely used to drive prestalk-specific reporter expression, and the protein contributes to the stalk-tube extracellular matrix during culmination.

acga.summary: ACG (adenylyl cyclase G) is one of the three Dictyostelium adenylyl cyclases. It is expressed in spores, where it acts as an osmosensor: high ambient osmolarity stimulates its cAMP production to keep spores dormant and inhibit premature germination.

acra.summary: ACR (also called ACB) is an adenylyl cyclase carrying sensor histidine-kinase-like and response-regulator domains. It is required during late development for proper culmination and terminal spore and stalk differentiation.

pkar.summary: Regulatory subunit of cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA). Without cAMP it binds and inhibits the PKA catalytic subunit (pkaC); cAMP binding releases the catalytic subunit. PKA activity is the master switch for aggregation, prestalk/prespore choice, and spore maturation.

gpab.summary: Galpha2, the heterotrimeric G-protein alpha subunit that couples the cAMP receptor cAR1 to downstream effectors during aggregation. gpaB-null cells fail to aggregate because they cannot transduce extracellular cAMP into intracellular responses.

gpba.summary: The single G-protein beta subunit in Dictyostelium. It partners with Galpha and Ggamma subunits to relay signaling from cAMP and folate receptors; gpbA-null cells are defective in chemotaxis and aggregation, showing that essentially all G-protein-mediated signaling routes through this one Gbeta.

daga.summary: CRAC (Cytosolic Regulator of Adenylyl Cyclase), a PH-domain protein that translocates to the plasma membrane by binding PIP3 produced on chemoattractant stimulation. It is required to activate the aggregation adenylyl cyclase ACA and is a classic live-cell reporter of PIP3 dynamics at the leading edge.
go: adenylate cyclase-activating G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway

piaa.summary: Pianissimo (PIA), a component of the TORC2 complex required to activate the aggregation adenylyl cyclase ACA in response to cAMP. piaA mutants cannot relay the cAMP signal and are aggregation-deficient.
go: adenylate cyclase-activating G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway

pika.summary: A class I phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase that, with related PI3Ks, generates PIP3 at the leading edge during chemotaxis. PI3K signaling, opposed by PTEN, helps establish cell polarity and directed movement up chemoattractant gradients.

pten.summary: The Dictyostelium ortholog of the PTEN lipid phosphatase. It dephosphorylates PIP3 and localizes to the rear and sides of chemotaxing cells, confining PIP3 to the leading edge; loss of PTEN broadens PIP3 signaling and impairs directional sensing.

pkba.summary: Protein kinase B (PKB/Akt), a PIP3-activated Ser/Thr kinase acting downstream of PI3K during chemotaxis to phosphorylate substrates that control cytoskeletal dynamics and directed migration.

yaka.summary: A DYRK-family Ser/Thr protein kinase governing the growth-to-development transition. yakA is required for cells to exit the cell cycle on starvation and initiate development, in part by relieving PufA-mediated translational repression of PKA.

pufa.summary: A Pumilio/PUF-family RNA-binding protein that translationally represses the PKA catalytic subunit (pkaC) mRNA during growth. Starvation, via yakA, relieves PufA repression, raising PKA activity to launch development.

dhka.summary: A two-component histidine kinase in the phosphorelay controlling culmination and spore maturation. DhkA responds to the peptide signal SDF-2 and feeds phosphate through the relay to RegA, modulating intracellular cAMP and triggering rapid spore encapsulation.

dhkb.summary: A two-component histidine kinase functioning in the phosphorelay that maintains spore dormancy. DhkB signaling, acting through RegA, keeps cAMP high in mature spores and prevents premature germination.

dhkc.summary: A two-component histidine kinase that links osmotic and ammonia cues to development, acting in the phosphorelay that sets the timing of culmination through control of intracellular cAMP via RegA.

rdea.summary: A histidine phosphotransfer (Hpt) protein that shuttles phosphate between sensor histidine kinases and the response regulator RegA. rdeA mutants ('rapid development') have low RegA activity, elevated cAMP, and accelerated development.

doka.summary: A hybrid histidine kinase/response-regulator mediating the response to hyperosmotic stress. DokA signaling raises intracellular cAMP and activates PKA to protect cells against osmotic shock.

rasc.summary: A Ras-family small GTPase acting early in chemoattractant signaling. RasC is rapidly and transiently activated at the leading edge on cAMP stimulation and is required for full activation of the adenylyl cyclase ACA and for efficient chemotaxis.

rapa.summary: The Dictyostelium Rap1 small GTPase, a key regulator of cell adhesion and cortical mechanics during chemotaxis. Active Rap1 at the leading edge promotes substrate adhesion and cytoskeletal remodeling and is tightly controlled by GEFs and GAPs to maintain polarity.

gefa.summary: A Ras guanine-nucleotide exchange factor (RasGEF), originally identified as 'aimless'. GefA activates the Ras signaling needed to stimulate the aggregation adenylyl cyclase ACA; gefA mutants are aggregation-deficient and chemotax poorly.

race.summary: A Rho-family small GTPase required for cytokinesis. RacE organizes the cortical actin cytoskeleton that maintains cortical tension and completes cleavage-furrow ingression; racE-null cells fail cytokinesis and become large and multinucleate.

rac1a.summary: A Rac-family Rho GTPase controlling actin-driven protrusion. Rac1A cycles between GDP- and GTP-bound states to regulate pseudopod and lamellipod formation, phagocytosis, and macropinocytosis at the cell front.

abpa.summary: Alpha-actinin, a calcium-regulated actin-crosslinking protein that bundles actin filaments and contributes to cortical actin organization and cell shape. Like several Dictyostelium crosslinkers it is partially redundant, so single mutants have mild phenotypes.

abpc.summary: Gelation factor (ABP-120/filamin), an actin-crosslinking protein that organizes orthogonal actin networks in the cortex and pseudopods. It supports pseudopod formation and motility; mutants show reduced cortical integrity and chemotaxis defects.

cora.summary: Coronin, a WD40-repeat actin-binding protein that localizes to the leading edge and dynamic actin structures and regulates actin turnover during motility, phagocytosis, and cytokinesis; corA mutants are defective in these actin-dependent processes.

forh.summary: A Diaphanous-related formin that nucleates and elongates unbranched actin filaments at filopodia and other protrusions, contributing to actin-based motility and cell-surface dynamics.

lime.summary: A small LIM-domain protein that associates with newly polymerized F-actin. A truncated LimE fused to a fluorescent protein is the most widely used live-cell reporter of dynamic actin in Dictyostelium, marking pseudopods, phagocytic cups, and the cytokinetic furrow.

arpb.summary: The Arp2 subunit of the Arp2/3 complex, which nucleates branched actin filaments. It drives the dendritic actin networks underlying pseudopods, phagocytic cups, and macropinocytic crowns.

cofa.summary: Cofilin, an actin-depolymerizing factor that severs and disassembles aged actin filaments to recycle monomers. Its activity supports the rapid actin turnover that powers Dictyostelium motility and chemotaxis.

daip1.summary: Actin-interacting protein 1 (Aip1), which cooperates with cofilin to cap and accelerate disassembly of cofilin-severed actin filaments, promoting the high filament turnover required for motility and cytokinesis.

myob.summary: A class I (single-headed, unconventional) myosin that links the actin cortex to membranes. Myosin IB localizes to the leading edge, phagocytic cups, and macropinosomes, contributing to pseudopod dynamics, phagocytosis, and cortical tension.

tala.summary: Talin A, a cytoskeletal adaptor that links the actin cortex to adhesion sites at the plasma membrane. It is required for normal substrate adhesion, traction, and phagocytosis; talA mutants show reduced adhesion and motility defects.

talb.summary: Talin B, a talin-family adaptor required during multicellular development. talB mutants form fragile slugs and fail to complete culmination, reflecting a role in the strong cell-substrate and cell-cell adhesion needed for morphogenesis.

siba.summary: A substrate-adhesion molecule of the SIB (similar to integrin beta) family, with an extracellular adhesion module and a cytoplasmic tail that binds talin to link the cell to the substratum; sibA mutants have reduced adhesion and phagocytosis.

phg1a.summary: Phg1A, a TM9-family transmembrane protein required for adhesion and phagocytosis. It controls cell-surface levels of the adhesion molecule SibA and is needed for efficient particle binding; phg1a mutants are defective in phagocytosis and in killing some bacteria.

srfa.summary: A MADS-box (SRF-like) transcription factor required for late spore differentiation. SrfA controls genes needed for prespore-to-spore maturation and spore-coat formation; srfA mutants produce defective, non-viable spores.

stka.summary: A GATA-family transcription factor ('stalky'). StkA promotes prespore-cell maintenance and proper stalk/spore proportioning; stkA mutants transdifferentiate excess prespore cells into stalk, yielding too few spores.

gtac.summary: A GATA-type transcription factor that decodes cAMP-pulse signaling during early development. GtaC shuttles dynamically in and out of the nucleus in response to oscillatory cAMP, coupling extracellular signaling to transcription of aggregation genes.

mybe.summary: A Myb-domain transcription factor involved in early development. mybE is required for normal expression of aggregation-stage genes and for timely entry into multicellular development.

dimb.summary: A basic-leucine-zipper (bZIP) transcription factor mediating responses to the stalk-inducing morphogen DIF-1. DimB rapidly translocates to the nucleus on DIF-1 exposure and regulates prestalk gene expression and cell-type proportioning.

cuda.summary: A nuclear regulator (CudA) required for culmination. Expressed in prestalk and prespore cells, it is needed for the cell-type-specific gene expression that permits fruiting-body formation; cudA mutants arrest at the slug stage.

rtoa.summary: RtoA (Ratio A), which regulates the proportion of prestalk to prespore cells by controlling cytosolic calcium and the timing of cell-type choice as cells enter development; rtoA mutants form fruiting bodies with altered spore:stalk ratios.

cotb.summary: A spore-coat protein (SP70) deposited in the outer spore coat during sporulation. cotB is a classic late prespore/spore marker whose promoter is widely used to drive spore-specific expression.
go: sporulation resulting in formation of a cellular spore

cotc.summary: A spore-coat protein (SP60) that, with other Cot proteins, assembles the protective spore coat. cotC is a canonical prespore/spore marker and a standard reporter for spore differentiation.
go: sporulation resulting in formation of a cellular spore

pspa.summary: A prespore-specific cell-surface glycoprotein (PsA/D19), one of the earliest and most widely used prespore markers; its expression marks commitment to the spore pathway during slug and culmination stages.
go: sporulation resulting in formation of a cellular spore

spia.summary: A late spore-differentiation protein expressed specifically during spore encapsulation. spiA is induced at the onset of sporulation and serves as a marker for terminal spore maturation.
go: sporulation resulting in formation of a cellular spore

ecmb.summary: An extracellular-matrix protein of the stalk tube (ST310/ecmB). ecmB is a prestalk/stalk-cell marker induced by the morphogen DIF-1, marking cells of the lower cup, stalk, and basal disc during culmination.

ctna.summary: Countin (CtnA), a component of the secreted Counting Factor complex that regulates aggregate size. Countin signaling breaks large streams into appropriately sized groups; ctnA mutants form abnormally large aggregates and fruiting bodies.

smla.summary: SmlA, a cytosolic protein that negatively regulates secretion of the Counting Factor. smlA mutants over-secrete Counting Factor and form small aggregates -- the opposite of countin mutants -- together defining the size-regulation pathway.

cula.summary: Cullin A, the scaffold of a Cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin-ligase complex. CulA-based ligases target proteins for ubiquitin-dependent degradation and are required for normal development, including the prestalk/prespore transition.

atg1.summary: Atg1, the Ser/Thr protein kinase that initiates autophagy. As part of the autophagy-induction complex it triggers autophagosome formation on starvation; autophagy is essential in Dictyostelium for surviving nutrient stress and for development.

atg8.summary: Atg8, a ubiquitin-like protein conjugated to phosphatidylethanolamine on the autophagosome membrane. Lipidated Atg8 marks growing autophagosomes and is the standard fluorescent reporter for monitoring autophagy in Dictyostelium.

carb.summary: cAMP receptor 2 (cAR2), a serpentine G-protein-coupled receptor for extracellular cAMP. cAR2 has lower cAMP affinity than cAR1 and is expressed at the mound stage in prestalk cells, where it helps transduce cAMP signals that pattern the multicellular structure.

carc.summary: cAMP receptor 3 (cAR3), a G-protein-coupled cAMP receptor expressed during early multicellular development. It contributes to cAMP relay and cell-type patterning, partly overlapping in function with the other cAMP receptors.

card.summary: cAMP receptor 4 (cAR4), the latest-expressed of the four cAMP receptors, present in prestalk and prespore cells during culmination. It fine-tunes the cAMP responses required for terminal differentiation and normal spore/stalk patterning.

gpaa.summary: Galpha1, a heterotrimeric G-protein alpha subunit. It is one of several Galpha subunits that couple cell-surface receptors to intracellular effectors; gpaA mutants show altered growth and development.

crla.summary: A cAMP-receptor-like (family-3 / GABA-B-type) G-protein-coupled receptor that broadens the GPCR repertoire beyond the four cAR receptors and contributes to developmental signaling.

gca.summary: A membrane-bound (12-transmembrane) guanylyl cyclase that produces cGMP in response to chemoattractant. With the soluble cyclase sGC it generates the cGMP burst that regulates myosin II assembly in the cell rear during chemotaxis.

sgca.summary: The soluble guanylyl cyclase (sGC), the major source of chemoattractant-stimulated cGMP. It localizes dynamically to the leading edge, and the cGMP it produces controls myosin II filament formation and suppression of lateral pseudopods during chemotaxis.

erkb.summary: A mitogen-activated protein kinase (Dd-ERK2). ERK2 is rapidly and transiently activated by cAMP and is required for the cAMP relay that drives aggregation; erkB-null cells are aggregation-deficient.

erka.summary: A mitogen-activated protein kinase (Dd-ERK1) acting in MAP-kinase signaling during growth and development, with roles distinct from the aggregation-essential ERK2.

meka.summary: A MAP kinase kinase (MEK) that phosphorylates and activates downstream MAP kinases, functioning in the signaling cascades that control aggregation and chemotaxis.

paka.summary: A p21-activated kinase (PAKa) acting downstream of Rac GTPases. PAKa localizes to the rear of chemotaxing cells and the cleavage furrow, where it promotes myosin II assembly and is required for normal cytokinesis and cell polarity.

ctxa.summary: Cortexillin I, an actin-bundling protein of the alpha-actinin/spectrin superfamily that concentrates in the cleavage furrow during cytokinesis. With cortexillin II it is essential for normal cell shape and division; double mutants fail cytokinesis.

ctxb.summary: Cortexillin II, an actin-bundling protein that partners with cortexillin I at the cleavage furrow to drive cytokinesis and maintain cortical mechanics and cell shape.

fima.summary: Fimbrin (plastin), a calcium-regulated actin-bundling protein. It crosslinks actin filaments in the cell cortex, filopodia, and phagocytic structures, contributing to cortical organization.

seva.summary: Severin, a calcium-activated, gelsolin-related protein that severs and caps actin filaments, promoting actin-filament turnover and remodeling during motility and other actin-dependent processes.

proa.summary: Profilin I, a small actin-monomer-binding protein that regulates the pool of polymerization-competent actin. Profilins I and II are partly redundant; loss of both severely disrupts the cytoskeleton and cytokinesis.

prob.summary: Profilin II, an actin-monomer-binding protein that, with profilin I, controls actin polymerization dynamics. The two profilins act redundantly to maintain cytoskeletal organization and normal cell division.

scra.summary: SCAR (WAVE), an activator of the Arp2/3 complex that nucleates branched actin filaments to build pseudopods and other protrusions; scrA mutants have abnormal cell shape and reduced motility. SCAR was originally identified in Dictyostelium.

wasa.summary: Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome protein (WASP), an activator of the Arp2/3 complex. WASP nucleates branched actin at sites of clathrin-mediated endocytosis, phagocytosis, and the leading edge, and is essential for viability.

vasp.summary: Ena/VASP, an actin-regulatory protein that localizes to filopodial tips and promotes actin-filament elongation. VasP is important for filopodia formation and contributes to chemotaxis and adhesion.

gmfa.summary: Glia maturation factor (GMF), an ADF-H-family protein that promotes debranching and disassembly of Arp2/3-nucleated actin networks, helping turn over branched actin during motility.

mlce.summary: The essential light chain of myosin II, which binds the myosin II heavy-chain neck and is required for motor function, supporting the myosin II activity needed for cytokinesis and cortical tension.

mlcr.summary: The regulatory light chain of myosin II. Its phosphorylation modulates myosin II motor activity and filament function during cytokinesis and cortical contraction.

mhka.summary: Myosin heavy-chain kinase A (MHCK A), an alpha-kinase that phosphorylates threonines in the myosin II tail to drive filament disassembly. It is a key regulator of myosin II localization and turnover during motility and cytokinesis.

myoi.summary: A class VII unconventional myosin required for cell-substratum adhesion and phagocytosis. Myosin VII works with talin to link the actin cytoskeleton to adhesion receptors and is needed for filopodia and particle uptake.

dyma.summary: Dynamin A, a large GTPase involved in membrane scission. DymA functions in endocytosis, organelle (including mitochondrial and contractile-vacuole) dynamics, and cytokinesis.

chca.summary: Clathrin heavy chain, the structural backbone of clathrin coats, required for clathrin-mediated endocytosis and vesicle traffic; chcA mutants have defects in endocytosis, osmoregulation, and development.

rab7a.summary: A Rab7 small GTPase that regulates late-endosomal and phagosomal maturation, controlling trafficking and acidification of phagosomes -- important for digestion of ingested bacteria.

tuba.summary: Alpha-tubulin, which heterodimerizes with beta-tubulin to form microtubules. Microtubules radiating from the centrosome organize the mitotic spindle and intracellular transport.

rasd.summary: A Ras-family small GTPase expressed strongly in prestalk cells during development. Constitutively active rasD disrupts pattern formation, indicating a role in developmental cell-fate signaling.

rass.summary: A Ras-family small GTPase that regulates fluid-phase endocytosis and motility. rasS mutants take up nutrients poorly and move abnormally, linking Ras signaling to macropinocytosis and growth.

gbpd.summary: A RasGEF-domain protein (cyclic-nucleotide-binding GEF family) that activates the small GTPase Rap1. GbpD signaling promotes cell spreading, substrate adhesion, and flattening; its loss reduces adhesion.

gska.summary: Glycogen synthase kinase-3 (GSK-3), a Ser/Thr kinase that regulates the stalk-versus-spore cell-fate choice. Activated downstream of cAMP via the tyrosine kinase ZAK1, GSK-3 promotes prespore over prestalk fate.

sgka.summary: A sphingosine kinase that phosphorylates sphingosine to sphingosine-1-phosphate, a bioactive sphingolipid. This lipid-kinase activity contributes to sphingolipid signaling affecting growth and stress responses.

ipla.summary: An inositol-1,4,5-trisphosphate-receptor-like protein, the principal intracellular calcium-release channel in Dictyostelium. iplA is required for calcium responses to chemoattractants and other agonists.

dsta.summary: Dd-STATa, a STAT-family transcription factor activated by extracellular cAMP via the receptor cAR1. It translocates to the nucleus and is required for proper culmination and stalk-cell differentiation; dstA mutants arrest as slugs.

dstc.summary: Dd-STATc, a STAT-family transcription factor activated by the morphogen DIF-1 and by stress (e.g. hyperosmotic). It accumulates in the nucleus to regulate prestalk and stress-response gene expression.

dmta.summary: Des-methyl-DIF-1 methyltransferase (DmtA), which catalyzes the final methylation step in synthesis of the stalk-inducing morphogen DIF-1. dmtA mutants lack DIF-1 and are impaired in prestalk/stalk differentiation.

stlb.summary: Steely2 (StlB), a hybrid polyketide-synthase/fatty-acid-synthase enzyme that produces the polyketide precursor of the morphogen DIF-1. stlB mutants lack DIF-1, linking this enzyme to stalk-cell induction.

tagb.summary: A prestalk-specific protein combining an ABC-transporter and a serine-protease domain. TagB processes and exports peptide signals (the SDF family) needed for prestalk-cell differentiation and culmination.

tagc.summary: A prestalk ABC-transporter/serine-protease that processes and releases the peptide signal SDF-2 to trigger rapid spore encapsulation during culmination.

cmfa.summary: Conditioned Medium Factor (CMF), a secreted glycoprotein that reports cell density. Starving cells release CMF, and only once enough accumulates (high density) can cells respond to cAMP and aggregate, coupling population density to development.

cada.summary: DdCAD-1 (gp24), a calcium-dependent cell-adhesion molecule that mediates the EDTA-sensitive cell contacts formed early in aggregation. It is secreted and transported to the cell surface to bind cells together at the onset of development.

rbla.summary: A retinoblastoma (Rb)-family protein that regulates the cell cycle and development, helping couple proliferation to the developmental program and influencing spore differentiation.

culb.summary: Cullin B, a scaffold subunit of a Cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin-ligase complex that targets proteins for ubiquitin-dependent degradation, contributing to developmental regulation.

dhkd.summary: A two-component histidine kinase that feeds into the phosphorelay controlling intracellular cAMP via RegA, contributing to the regulation of developmental timing.

gapa.summary: A Ras GTPase-activating protein (GAP) required for cytokinesis. GAPA helps recruit the cortexillins to the cleavage furrow; gapA mutants fail to divide and become large and multinucleate.

rgaa.summary: An IQGAP-related RasGAP-domain protein (DGAP1). With GAPA and the cortexillins it forms a cortical complex that controls cleavage-furrow formation and cell shape during cytokinesis.

pona.summary: Ponticulin, an integral membrane glycoprotein that is a major link between the plasma membrane and the cortical actin network, nucleating and binding actin filaments at the membrane.

coma.summary: Comitin, a membrane-associated, actin-binding protein found on Golgi and vesicle membranes that links them to the actin cytoskeleton and contributes to membrane trafficking and the response to stress.

vata.summary: The catalytic A subunit of the vacuolar (V-type) H+-ATPase. The V-ATPase pumps protons to acidify endosomes, lysosomes, and the contractile vacuole, driving osmoregulation and digestion of engulfed material.

vatb.summary: The B subunit of the vacuolar (V-type) H+-ATPase, part of the catalytic V1 sector. The V-ATPase acidifies endo-lysosomal compartments and the contractile vacuole for osmoregulation and digestion.

vatm.summary: The 100-kDa membrane subunit (subunit a) of the vacuolar (V-type) H+-ATPase membrane sector. It anchors the proton-pumping V0 domain in the membrane of the contractile vacuole and endo-lysosomal system.

psena.summary: A presenilin-family aspartyl protease, the catalytic core of gamma-secretase. Dictyostelium presenilins make it a model for presenilin function; they contribute to development, phagocytosis, and intramembrane proteolysis.

psenb.summary: A presenilin-family aspartyl protease that, with PsenA, provides the catalytic activity of gamma-secretase. Presenilin function in this model organism affects cell-fate determination and phagocytosis.

atg5.summary: Autophagy protein 5 (Atg5), part of the Atg12-Atg5/Atg16 conjugation system that drives autophagosome membrane expansion. Autophagy is required in Dictyostelium for surviving starvation and for development.

atg7.summary: Autophagy protein 7 (Atg7), an E1-like activating enzyme for the two ubiquitin-like conjugation systems (Atg8 and Atg12) that build autophagosomes. atg7 mutants are autophagy-deficient and impaired in development.

atg9.summary: Autophagy protein 9 (Atg9), the only multi-spanning transmembrane core autophagy protein. It delivers membrane to the forming autophagosome during the autophagic response to starvation.

tipd.summary: Atg16 (the 'tipD' tipped-aggregate mutant). With the Atg12-Atg5 conjugate it forms the complex that specifies the site of autophagosome membrane expansion; tipD mutants are autophagy-defective and arrest with a tipped-aggregate phenotype.

apra.summary: AprA (Autocrine Proliferation Repressor A), a secreted protein that accumulates with cell density and slows proliferation, so cells divide more slowly as the population grows. It acts together with CfaD and signals through a G-protein/GPCR pathway.
go: negative regulation of cell population proliferation

cfad.summary: CfaD, a secreted cathepsin-like protein required for the activity of the chalone AprA. Together AprA and CfaD form an autocrine signal that represses proliferation as cell density rises.
go: negative regulation of cell population proliferation

cfaa.summary: A counting-factor-associated protein, part of the secreted Counting Factor complex (with countin) that regulates aggregate size by breaking large cell streams into appropriately sized groups.

amta.summary: An ammonium transporter. Ammonia produced by the cells is a developmental signal, and Amt transporters modulate its distribution to influence slug phototaxis and the timing of culmination.

amtb.summary: An ammonium transporter contributing to the ammonia signaling that regulates the slug-migration-versus-culmination decision during multicellular development.

amtc.summary: An ammonium transporter implicated in slug phototaxis and thermotaxis and in the control of culmination, through its effect on intracellular ammonium and the ammonia developmental signal.

cycb.summary: Cyclin B, the mitotic cyclin that activates the cyclin-dependent kinase to drive entry into mitosis. Its periodic accumulation and destruction help time cell division.

pldb.summary: A phospholipase D that hydrolyzes membrane phospholipids to generate phosphatidic acid, a lipid second messenger; PLD signaling influences membrane trafficking and the cytoskeleton.

plaa.summary: A patatin-family phospholipase A that releases fatty acids from membrane phospholipids, contributing to lipid signaling and membrane remodeling.

pakc.summary: A p21-activated kinase (PAK) acting downstream of Rac GTPases to regulate the actin and myosin cytoskeleton during motility and chemotaxis.

phg2.summary: Phg2, a ROCO-family Ser/Thr protein kinase required for cell-substrate adhesion and phagocytosis. It regulates actin distribution at the cell cortex and the contact site with particles.

rab8a.summary: A Rab8 small GTPase that regulates exocytic and post-Golgi vesicle traffic to the plasma membrane and the contractile vacuole, supporting secretion and membrane delivery.

rab11a.summary: A Rab11 small GTPase that controls recycling-endosome traffic and delivery of membrane to the cell surface, the phagosome, and the contractile vacuole.

nxna.summary: Annexin VII (synexin), a calcium- and phospholipid-binding protein associated with membranes. It binds membranes in a calcium-dependent way and is implicated in membrane organization and calcium homeostasis.

aara.summary: Aardvark, a beta-catenin/armadillo-family protein. It functions in the GSK-3 pathway controlling the stalk-versus-spore cell-fate decision and also contributes to cell-cell junctions in the tip epithelium.

abca1.summary: An ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter. ABC transporters couple ATP hydrolysis to the movement of substrates across membranes.
